clue.text: Handsome fellow found among bald mounties every now and then

indicators.note: every now and then says take letters at regular intervals, here every second one of these two words

explanation.surface: A good-looking man turns up among a bald squad of Canadian police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of 'bald mounties'; Mounties are Canada's mounted police.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Aphrodite loved this beautiful youth, so his name stands for any very good-looking man.

clue.text: Virtually worthless chap tried reforming

indicators.note: re-forming means shaping again, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A fellow who attempted to change his ways is now of little value.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sold for next to nothing is very low in price, close to valueless.

clue.text: Puzzle bringing no new benefit

parts.note: a plus is an advantage or benefit

explanation.surface: A brainteaser that brings no fresh advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle or perplex someone is to puzzle them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Canadian city presently welcomes a runner in winter (not European)

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the word for presently holds the next pieces

parts.note: presently means soon, before long

indicators.note: not says the European letter is dropped from the runner

parts.note: a skate glides over ice in winter, its blade being a runner

explanation.surface: A town in Canada will shortly host a racer in the cold season, though none from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: A skate's blade is called a runner, hence 'runner in winter'; 'not European' leaves SKAT, which 'welcomes' tucks inside the word for presently.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a city in the prairie province of Saskatchewan, so a Canadian city by name.

clue.text: Asian girl one accompanies on mountain

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means coming after the mountain word

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
gal is an informal word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A young woman, with a companion, climbs a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accompanies' simply joins the girl and the one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bengali is a person from Bengal, a region of South Asia, so an Asian by origin.

clue.text: Britain beset by ugly landscapes?

definitions.meaning: an affectionate old soldiers' name for Britain, from Hindi
a playful made-up adjective meaning full of blight, eyesores that spoil a view

explanation.surface: The country is plagued by unsightly views.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading coins a jokey adjective from blight plus the suffix -y, as in full of blight; the question mark flags the invention.
explanation.definitionFit: British soldiers in India used this nickname for home, and it still affectionately names Britain.

clue.text: Extremely valuable information about Israel territory

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the joined pieces are read backwards
extremely points to the extreme letters, first and last, of valuable

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Some very precious intelligence concerning Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but turns the whole of VEGEN round; 'gen' is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: This desert region forms the southern part of Israel, so it is Israeli territory.

clue.text: Stop sailor heading off from Gdansk perhaps?

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the next word is removed

parts.note: Gdansk is a city in Poland, so something from there is Polish; perhaps marks an example

explanation.surface: A seaman setting off from a Polish port is told to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops P from POLISH, leaving OLISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To do away with a practice or law is to put an end to it, a verb synonym of halt.

clue.text: Music welcomed by certain trombonists

indicators.note: welcomed by says the answer is held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some brass players greet a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening passage of a song is the introductory music, so it is a piece of music.

clue.text: Jewellery item displayed back to front makes you smile

indicators.note: the last letter of the jewellery word is shown at its front instead

parts.note: a ring is an item of jewellery worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery worn the wrong way round brings a smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' tempts a full reversal (GNIR), but only the back letter G moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad smile showing the teeth is this word's ordinary meaning, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: More than one fairground ride wasn't so big after reconstruction

indicators.note: something rebuilt has its parts put together anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebuilt fairground attraction turns out smaller than it was before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than one' tells you the answer is plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Swingboats are boat-shaped swings seen at British fairs, a fairground ride in plural form.

clue.text: Going round cape, friend's repulsed sea monster

indicators.note: going round says the friend's word surrounds the cape letter
repulsed means driven back, so the friend's word is read backwards

parts.note: an ally is a friend, and the possessive adds S
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: Sailing round a headland, a friend fights off a monster of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repulsed' turns ALLYS into SYLLA, which wraps round C.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this many-headed creature lurked opposite Charybdis, devouring sailors from passing ships.

clue.text: Broadcast e.g. favourite show on telly finally — this one?

definitions.text: Broadcast e.g. favourite show on telly finally — this one?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order
finally picks the last letter of the word telly

explanation.surface: Someone's favourite television programme is put out on air, perhaps this very one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'this one?' points to a long-running BBC satirical news quiz whose title is hidden in the jumble of 'e.g. favourite show on' plus Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes a favourite telly show being broadcast, and the BBC panel quiz is just such a programme.

clue.text: See 12
Quickly introduced us in this place, with lots of noise

parts.note: here means in this place
a din is a loud continuous noise

explanation.surface: Someone hurried us in here amid a great racket.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone in, as an usher does, is to lead or admit them promptly, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Carry explosive a short distance

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive
ft, short for foot, is a small distance

explanation.surface: Someone transports a bomb only a little way.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift or bear something weighty is a verb sense of this word, matching carry.

clue.text: Monk, some people mistakenly say, showing criminal tendencies

indicators.note: some speakers pronounce th as f, so the jazz name is said with an f sound

parts.note: Thelonious Monk was an American jazz pianist

explanation.surface: A monk is described, wrongly some say, as being inclined to crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monk' looks like a religious brother, but it is the jazz pianist's surname giving his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A felony is a serious crime, so the adjective describes wicked, criminal conduct.

clue.text: Executive producer principally in charge of film

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so take the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A senior producer is mainly responsible for a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, grand-scale movie is called by this name, so it is one kind of film.

clue.text: Two pounds in change for a dictionary?

indicators.note: in says the two letters go inside the change word

parts.note: change in your pocket means coins
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), so two pounds is LL

explanation.surface: Is two pounds in loose change the price of a dictionary?
explanation.definitionFit: This publisher's English dictionary is well known, so the name stands for a dictionary, flagged by the question mark.

clue.text: Around eleven old pennies for crackers?

definitions.meaning: a pre-1971 British ... was worth twelve old pennies, so eleven or so falls short of one
crackers is British slang for mad, slightly unhinged

explanation.surface: Eleven old pence is offered as the price for some crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom for someone a bit simple or mad says they are short of a whole coin; the shilling was worth twelve old pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: A person said to fall short of a whole coin is mentally lacking, hence slang for mad or dim.

clue.text: A record label first appearing in Filipino language

indicators.note: first says the label word comes ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: a tag is a label
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A record label releases its first album in a Philippine tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the main language of the Philippines, the basis of the national tongue Filipino.

clue.text: In fact, a terrible bigot

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: In truth, someone is an awful bigot.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot with extreme, intolerant views is an obsessive, close in sense to a bigot.

clue.text: See 19
Bird — male — appearing south of river

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below the river letter

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
on means appearing, as a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: A male bird is spotted south of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes, so this is a type of bird.

clue.text: Edition of magazine Children Matter

definitions.meaning: one number of a periodical published at a given time
a legal word for offspring, as in died without children
a point or topic under discussion, a subject

explanation.surface: An edition of a magazine called Children Matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A single word that means a magazine number, offspring, and a topic for debate.

clue.text: Fights knight in what's left of old castle?

indicators.note: in says the knight letter goes inside the remains

parts.note: ruins are the remains of a ruined old building such as a castle
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight battles among the crumbling remains of an old castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's left' looks like a deletion signal, but it is the definition of RUINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-ins are quarrels or brushes with someone, informal words for fights or clashes.

clue.text: Healthy dessert? Foreign frau's boy will consume it

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so the frau's word and the boy surround the next word
foreign suggests strangeness, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A German wife's son will eat up a nourishing pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' gives FRUSA from the frau's letters; 'will consume' means that jumble plus the boy swallows 'it'. Frau is German for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of mixed chopped fruit is a dessert, and a wholesome one, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Excessively large wrench maybe

parts.note: too means excessively, as in too big
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An oversized spanner.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is one example of a hand implement, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Teens collected a couple of grand in savings for the future

indicators.note: collected here means gathered up and reassembled, so the letters are rearranged
a couple of means two, so the letter is written twice

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Teenagers have gathered a couple of thousand as a fund for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Money put aside for later use is a reserve fund, the idiomatic sense of this phrase.

clue.text: Most attractive aspect of Venice's trattorias

indicators.note: aspect of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The most charming thing about Venice is its little restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of nice: the pleasantest, most pleasing or appealing one of a set.
